Interesting historical audio: President Lyndon Johnson strong-arms Senator Richard Russell

I like this audio not just for the interesting historical context of LBJ putting together the Warren Commission shortly after JFK's assassination, but for the way they talk. You really don't hear these old southern accents and speech mannerisms anymore, especially things that seem a little shocking today, hearing the President and a senator casually drop the words "negro" and "nigger" (around 10:23 in the video).

My favorite part (and the part I found the funniest) is when Sen. Russell complains that he can't serve on the commission because he "doesn't have the time" on top of his normal Georgia items and LBJ sarcastically mocks him for it, saying (paraphrasing) "Oh well, alright then, I guess we'll just make the time then, won't we?" How does it feel to be so domesticated, honestly? Did you see your life being so normal? How old are you

I am 31. Honestly? It depends on the day. I used to be a wild and crazy guy riding motorcycles and driving sports cars. At some point I realized I wasn't invulnerable and decided to tone it down and stick to "safer" hobbies like wrenching on cars, building computers, and shooting guns. This lead to a consistent work quality and career which lead to marriage. Marriage lead to homeownership. After 5 years of marriage and owning a home we decided that maybe kids would be fun but we weren't really ready. Less than a year later we were pregnant.

Now with 2 kids I can't be too nutty so we take things as they come. My kids think I am the wildest and craziest because I do all of those gender stereotypical dad things but I am fairly tame. My dad wasn't around a lot when I was a kid so I make sure I am there for my kids.

We recently moved from CT to Florida from the woods to a neighborhood which makes me feel even more domesticated. I have no issues with my life because when things changed I was ready to face the challenges and rise to the occasion.

Do you view being domesticated as negative for yourself?

Edit: Almost forgot. It depends on the day because sometimes I miss the freedom from so much responsibility but not so much that I would give up my family.

Edit: I never planned on having kids but planned on marriage and house. So yes. I did see myself being exactly what I am. I did not plan on living in Florida either but here I am.
